$comment: The must-never layer for interface honesty. Eight of these nine are forbidden and non-exemptible: a project may not except them, because the thing being prohibited is telling the user something untrue, and there is no project in which that is a reasonable trade. Identity is frozen by artifacts/design/rule-catalog-v1.md.

rules.title: Design artifacts and the implementation do not contradict each other
rules.description: Where design artifacts exist, they describe the interface that ships. A divergence is resolved or recorded, not left for a reader to discover.
rules.rationale: A stale design document is worse than none: it is consulted, believed, and acted on. Its cost is paid by whoever trusted it.
rules.remediation: Update the artifact, or record the divergence and which side is authoritative.
rules.$assuranceNote: Presence and structure of an artifact is checkable. Whether its content matches the shipped interface is not, and this rule does not claim it is.

rules.title: The interface does not manipulate its user
rules.description: The interface does not use design to push a user toward a choice against their interest: no confusing opt-outs, no manufactured urgency, no obstruction of the path the user is actually looking for.
rules.rationale: A manipulated choice is not a choice. An interface that works by defeating its user's intent has stopped being a tool.
rules.remediation: Present the options with equal clarity and let the choice be made on its merits.
rules.$assuranceNote: Manipulation is defined by intent and effect, neither of which is present in source. Only a human establishes this, and only for what they reviewed.

rules.title: Failure is not presented as success
rules.description: An operation that failed is not reported to the user as having succeeded, and an operation still in progress is not reported as complete.
rules.rationale: A false success is the most damaging thing an interface can do, because the user stops watching. Every subsequent decision they make is built on a fact that is not true.
rules.remediation: Report the failure with what happened and what the user can do about it.
rules.$assuranceNote: Establishing this needs a failing operation driven in a browser and the resulting interface observed. It is evaluated for the failure paths a run actually provoked.

rules.title: Progress indication corresponds to real progress
rules.description: A determinate progress indicator reflects measured progress. An animation on a timer is not presented as a measurement.
rules.rationale: A progress bar is a claim about how much is done and how long remains. Inventing that claim trades the user's ability to plan for the appearance of responsiveness.
rules.remediation: Use an indeterminate indicator where progress is unknown, and a determinate one only where it is measured.
rules.$assuranceNote: Whether a number is a measurement is a question about the work it claims to describe, not about the code that renders it. A value driven by a timer, a value computed on a server, and a value derived from real progress are the same expression at the call site, and a running interface shows a bar advancing without disclosing what fraction is genuinely done. Only a reviewer who knows what the operation does can establish this, and only for what they reviewed. Re-typed from code-analysis before v1.0.0 — see ADR 0014.

rules.title: Unavailable capability is not presented as available
rules.description: A feature that does not exist, is not enabled for this user, or cannot currently work is not presented as though it can be used.
rules.rationale: A user who spends effort reaching a capability that was never available has been charged for a promise the interface had no basis to make.
rules.remediation: Remove the affordance, or show it in a state that says what is required to make it available.
rules.$assuranceNote: Whether a presented capability is genuinely available depends on entitlement, configuration, and backend state that no scan of the interface can establish.

rules.title: A control that does nothing is not presented as a control
rules.description: An element styled and labeled as an interactive control performs an action when activated, or is shown in a state that says why it cannot.
rules.rationale: An inert control costs the user a decision, an action, and then the time to work out whether the failure was theirs.
rules.remediation: Wire the control, remove it, or give it a disabled state with a reason.
rules.$assuranceNote: Inertness is established by activating the control and observing that nothing happened. That is a browser property, and only for controls a run actually activated.

rules.title: Placeholder and invented data are not shipped as real
rules.description: Sample values, lorem ipsum, hard-coded example figures, and invented records are not presented to a user as the product's real data.
rules.rationale: A user cannot tell placeholder data from real data. Shipping it means shipping a number someone may act on.
rules.remediation: Bind the view to real data, or show an empty state that says there is nothing yet.
rules.$assuranceNote: The detector recognises well-known placeholder signatures. Plausible invented data is indistinguishable from real data in source, which is exactly what makes it dangerous.

rules.title: Destructive consequence is not obscured
rules.description: An action that destroys data or is otherwise irreversible says so before it is taken, in terms that name what will be lost.
rules.rationale: Consent to a consequence requires knowing the consequence. Destruction described as 'continue' was not consented to.
rules.remediation: Name the object and the consequence in the confirmation, and make the destructive choice the deliberate one.
rules.$assuranceNote: Whether a consequence is adequately disclosed is a reading of the interface's language in context. A human establishes it.

rules.title: Visual evidence is not weakened to make a check pass
rules.description: Baselines, thresholds, and review scope are not loosened so that a failing visual check reports success.
rules.rationale: Weakening the check does not change the interface; it changes what the project is willing to know about the interface. That is the failure this framework exists to prevent, applied to itself.
rules.remediation: Fix the regression, or record the accepted change as a deliberate baseline update with its reason.
rules.$assuranceNote: A baseline update is legitimate or not depending on intent, which is established by review of the change and its justification, never by the diff alone.
